findings.title: Executes shell commands
findings.why: Shell access turns a data source into an actor. Once the model can pass a string to a shell, argument injection becomes command injection and the tool description becomes the trust boundary.
findings.fix: Use an allowlist, avoid `shell: true`, and quote interpolated values.
findings.evidence: """Execute a shell command""" return subprocess.check_output(command, shell=True).decode

findings.title: Dependency ranges that can float
findings.why: A caret or star range means today’s install and tomorrow’s install can be different code. For a component that holds credentials and runs commands, that is unearned trust.
findings.fix: Pin exact versions, or at minimum commit a lockfile and install with `npm ci`.
